title: Pyrimidine Nucleotide Metabolism
objectives: Trace the de novo biosynthesis pathway of pyrimidines
Compare regulation of CAD and UMP synthase enzymes
Explain the salvage pathway and catabolism of pyrimidines

overview.title: Pyrimidine Metabolism Overview
overview.content:
Nucleotide Production Pathways

  • De novo synthesis: Builds nucleotides from simple precursors (carbamoyl-P, Asp, PRPP)
  • Salvage pathway: Recycles free bases/nucleosides
  • Shared precursors: Ribose-5-P (PRPP), CO2, Glu/Asp (N donors)

digestion.title: Dietary Nucleic Acid Digestion
digestion.content:
Intestinal Processing

Enzymatic Breakdown

  • Pancreatic nucleases → oligonucleotides
  • Phosphodiesterases → mononucleotides (3'/5')
  • Nucleotidases → nucleosides + Pi
  • Nucleosidases → free bases + ribose
  • Dietary purines are excreted as uric acid

de_novo.title: De Novo Pyrimidine Synthesis
de_novo.content:
6-Step Biosynthesis (Cytosol)

1. Carbamoyl-P Formation

  • CO2 + glutamine + 2ATP → carbamoyl-P (CPS-II)
  • Committed step (inhibited by UTP, activated by PRPP)

2-3. CAD Complex Reactions

  • Carbamoyl-P + Asp → carbamoyl aspartate (ATCase)
  • → Dihydroorotate (DHOase)
  • Regulation: CTP inhibits, ATP activates

4. Orotate Formation (Mitochondria)

  • Dihydroorotate → orotate (DHODH, FMN/Q-dependent)
  • Only redox step (links to ETC)

5-6. UMP Production

  • Orotate + PRPP → OMP (OPRT)
  • OMP → UMP (OMP decarboxylase)
  • Bifunctional enzyme: UMP synthase

CTP & TMP Synthesis

  • CTP: UTP + glutamine + ATP → CTP (CTP synthetase)
  • TMP: dUMP + N5,N10-methylene-THF → TMP (thymidylate synthase)
  • THF regeneration: DHF reductase (MTX target)

regulation.title: Pathway Regulation
regulation.content:
Control Mechanisms

CAD Complex

  • CPS-II: UTP (-), PRPP/ATP (+)
  • ATCase: CTP (-), ATP (+)

UMP Synthase

  • Coordinated repression/derepression with CAD

PRPP Availability

  • Synthesized by PRPP synthetase (X-linked)
  • Activated by Pi, inhibited by ADP

catabolism.title: Pyrimidine Catabolism
catabolism.content:
Degradation Pathway

Stepwise Breakdown

  • Nucleotidases → nucleosides
  • Nucleoside phosphorylases → bases + ribose-1-P
  • Dehydrogenation (uracil/thymine)
  • Ring opening (hydratase)
  • Final deamination/decarboxylation (β-ureidopropionase)

disorders.title: Clinical Disorders
disorders.content:
Orotic Aciduria

Causes

  • Type 1: UMP synthase deficiency (OPRT/OMP decarboxylase)
  • Type 2: OTC deficiency (urea cycle defect)
  • Acquired: Allopurinol competition, Reye syndrome

Clinical Features

  • Orotic acid accumulation (blood/urine)
  • Megaloblastic anemia (impaired DNA synthesis)
  • Hyperammonemia (in OTC-related cases)

Management

  • Uridine supplementation (bypasses block)
  • Supports salvage pathway nucleotide production

faqs.title: FAQs
faqs.content:
FAQs

Q: Why does OTC deficiency cause orotic aciduria? +

A: Mitochondrial carbamoyl-P accumulates when OTC is deficient, overflowing into the pyrimidine pathway where CPS-II utilizes it for excessive orotate production.

Q: How does uridine treat orotic aciduria? +

A: Uridine is salvaged to UMP, which inhibits CAD (feedback) and provides pyrimidines for DNA/RNA synthesis, bypassing the defective de novo pathway.

Q: Why is thymidylate synthase a chemotherapy target? +

A> It's the sole pathway for dTMP synthesis. Inhibitors (5-FU) deplete thymidine nucleotides, blocking DNA replication in rapidly dividing cancer cells.
